name: Vedanta Retreat, Olema
aka: Vedanta Society of Northern California Retreat
about: The Vedanta Retreat in Olema is a secluded 2,000-acre property on the Point Reyes Peninsula operated by the Vedanta Society of Northern California, a center of the Ramakrishna Order. Purchased in 1946 and open to overnight retreatants since 1973, it provides a quiet, largely pristine setting where spiritual seekers of any faith may devote themselves to serious study, prayer, and meditation. There are no scheduled classes or activities for overnight retreatants; each person plans and undertakes their own retreat in silence and solitude. Separate Men's and Women's Retreat Houses, a Meditation Room, a library, and three outdoor meditation sites support the practice. The retreat also hosts an annual interfaith Memorial Day program, Saturday spiritual discussions with a swami, and a spring youth forum.
technique: Self-directed meditation, contemplation, prayer, and spiritual study in the Vedanta tradition; no set method imposed.
teacherAccess: No scheduled teaching during overnight retreats; new candidates have an in-person interview beforehand, and swamis lead occasional Saturday spiritual discussions.
retreatOptions: Individual self-guided silent retreats of 1 to 5 days in the Men's or Women's Retreat Houses, not more than once a month.
schedule: Unstructured and self-planned; retreatants observe silence and solitude with no organized daily program.
cost: No charge to use the retreat; voluntary donations toward upkeep are welcomed.

pricePerDay.notes: No charge for use of the retreat; donation-only with no suggested amount.

foodNotes: No meals are served to overnight retreatants; they provide and prepare their own food, and only vegetarian food is permitted on the property.
workNotes: No work or service is required of overnight retreatants; the retreat is entirely self-directed.
